description: Every hull in the province, in one kit — the three watercraft families the catalogue reaches through `boats-keeled`, `boats-raft-canoe` and `plank-ferry-swamp`/`rowboats` (`boat.mixed.watercraft`, `boat.argonian.native-craft`, `boat.mixed.vault-boat-mods`). Boats are free-standing props, not a snapping tileset, so combining sources here breaks no author's system; what matters is that the CULTURE bands stay separate when placed. Band 1 NATIVE (keel-less, poled or paddled — the default Argonian craft): the SFSS dugout canoe with its oar/punt-pole props, the poled ferry raft with its plank pieces, and the flat plank ferries. Band 2 FOREIGN KEELED (Imperial, Nord, Breton, Redguard hulls — read as outsiders, so confine to Imperial ports, the Topal coast and pirate anchorages): the Cyrodiilic galleon, navy and trade ships, the Nord and Breton hulls, the sailboat family in intact and furled-sail variants. Band 3 WRECKS AND WORKS: the broken rowboats, the beached Nord trade ship, the ghost ship, and the bare `imperialship01base` hull. NOTE the bare hull is the answer to the shipyard `hull-on-stocks` gap the deliverability audit records as unsourceable: this resource ships the galleon's hull and its mast assembly as SEPARATE meshes, so a hull standing mastless on works-v1 stockade scaffold is authored geometry, not a kitbash of a piece nobody made. Two duplicate sources are deliberate: BM&V bundles the same Cyrodiil resource meshes, and we take the BM&V copies where they carry plugin dimensions, crediting the original (pool `impships`) as well. EXCLUDED, all for the same reason — an editor marker baked into the shipped mesh: `plank_ferry_swamp_02/04/05/06` and `boatmarker` (marker only, no hull at all); `river_ferry_haafingar_01`; and the WHOLE `boatsanim` pool (`boatcarrierdefault/ferry/02`), whose hulls each carry an untextured EditorMarker sub-mesh that vets as a solid slab. Removing it would mean editing another author's mesh, so the pool stays registered and credited and the gap is shown rather than faked. The moored-boat motion reference we wanted from it is served instead by `shiprowboatanim01`, which bobs and is clean. Also excluded: the SFSS skeleton/highlandcow rig files, which are not boats.

snapLogic.placement: Hulls are placed, not snapped. Each mesh's origin is at its own waterline-ish base; sit it on the water plane and let the mooring rope/cleat from docks-v1 do the tying. `shiprowboatanim01` (rowboats pool) carries its own NiControllerSequence bobbing motion and is the reference for moored-boat motion — the only clean animated hull we own.
snapLogic.sailing-variants: Ships and Boats of Tamriel ships each hull twice, `_docked` and `_sailing` (sails furled vs set); the sailboats pool does the same with plain vs `furled` names. Pick ONE per placement — they are alternative states of the same vessel, never two boats.
snapLogic.scale: Bethesda units; 0.0142240 m/unit. The galleon hull is ~29 m and the mast assembly ~33 m; the canoe and plank ferries are 4–6 m. Measured extents in watercraft-v1.kit.json.
